en: The Praise of the Essential Meaning of Vajrayoginī, composed by the Siddhācārya Virūpāda. Om! Homage to Vajrayoginī!
Oṃ, homage to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha. Oṃ, homage to the Gurus, Buddhas, and Bodhisattvas.
Oṃ, homage to Locanā and the other ten Vajravilāsinīs.
Homage to the ten heroic deities beginning with Yamāntaka!
Vārāhī, Śauṇḍinī, Caṇḍālī, and likewise Ḍombinī;
Naṭanī, Rajakī, Brāhmī, and Kapālinī—these are eternal. (1)
She is Amṛtā and Amṛtakuṇḍalī, the illuminator of the light of knowledge;
she alone is the Great Bliss among all the heroic goddesses of every direction.
And this emptiness is sung as the supreme power (parāśakti), higher than the highest;
it is the immortal, upward-moving, divine means that flows eternally. (3)
Khecarī, Bhūcarī, and likewise Pātālavāsinī;
Praviṣṭhāpūraṇī, who is eternally the agitatress (or terrifier) of the three worlds. || 4 ||
The Goddess consists of bindu, nāda, and kalā; she is indeed of the nature of the moon and the sun.
She is the eternal one, the emanation body, the enjoyment body, and the one of great bliss. || 5 ||
Transcending the bindu, nāda, and kalā, she is considered the Perfection of Wisdom;
for she is the intrinsic nature of all phenomena, yet devoid of all phenomena. (6)
She is devoid of dissolution and origination, yet she brings about dissolution and origination;
she is said to be established due to her eternity, yet she is free from that which is eternal.
It is embraced by profundity, sublime, of great significance, characterized by one's own resolute conviction, free from the three kinds of emptiness, and having the nature of luminosity. || 8 ||
She has the form of the single syllable *E* and is joined with the syllable *Vaṃ*;
she is endowed with the various moments beginning with *Vicitra*, and her nature is the fourfold bliss.
She also flashes forth within the external maṇḍala-circle from the three bodies;
she is the ornament of body, speech, and mind within the states of body, speech, and mind. (10)
Having transcended body, speech, and mind, and abiding in equanimity, the Goddess, whose form is selflessness, is established in suchness. (11)
She is the embodiment of the three voids, treading upon the lotus and the vajra; through the union of *lalanā* and *rasanā*, she is *avadhūtī*, the Great Bliss. (12)
And this dependent origination is the means for crossing over saṃsāra for both them and those [women];
having obtained this Yoginī, they are liberated from the bonds of worldly existence. (13)

Thus, this Yoginī has been declared to be the bestower of supernatural powers (ṛddhi) and the bestower of perfection (siddhi), as well as the supreme gateway to liberation for those who practice constantly. || 14 ||
She makes the body like a diamond and bestows the accomplishment of the elixir;
this Vajrayoginī is obtained through the grace of the Guru’s feet. 15.
By the mere recitation of this [text], the yogi, constantly filled with the equipment of knowledge, reverently attains the equipment of merit. (16)
In the *Śrīguhyasamayatantrotpattikramasādhana*, the sixteen verses summarizing the essential meaning (*piṇḍārtha*) by the Vajrayoginī of the Three Bodies are completed.
This work is the composition of the accomplished master, the venerable Virūpāda.
